To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
children with severe immunosuppession had lower frequencies of recent thymnic emigrant CD4 + T cells compared with those without evidence of immunodeficiency.

(i) the frequency of RTE T cells was higher in HIV‐inflicted children without evidence of immune suppression; (ii) the frequency of these cells was higher in children with a good rate of adherence to ART; and (iii) a good adherence to ART was associated with an increase in the frequency of RTE naïve CD8+ T cells.
the adequate ART adherence is crucial for immune reconstitution and might be reflected by levels of RTE CD 4 + T cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the association between ART adherence and the levels of RTE naïve CD T cells in children infected with HIV‐1.
the association between ART adherence and the frequency of RTE naïve CD 4+ T cells, which may be a potential marker of the immune reconstitution process in children with HIV‐1 infection.
the importance of the thymus for immune recovery in HIV‐inflected children.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the frequency of RTE cells in HIV‐1‐infected children is related to ART adherence and to the immune reconstitution.
the frequency of RTE cells is an indirect marker of ART adherence and is associated with CD4+ T‐cell restoration in HIV‐inflected children.
the frequency of RTE naïve CD+ T cells in patients with a high rate ART adherence is significantly higher than in patients with suboptimal ART adherence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the adequate ART adherence is important for immune reconstitution that might be reflected by levels of RTE CD 4 + T cells.
the frequency of RTE T cells was lower among children with severe immunosuppession, but the frequency was significantly higher among those with a high rate than those with suboptimial adherence.

the frequency of RTE cells in the blood of HIV‐infected subjects with no evidence of HIV‐related immunosuppression is similar to the levels of RTE cells in HIV‐uninfected children, suggesting that the thymus is able to maintain its function during the asymptomatic phase of infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the levels of RTE naïve CD+ T cells can be used as a marker of the efficacy of ART in HIV‐infused children.
the frequency of RTE naïve CD+ T cells can be used as a surrogate marker to evaluate ART adherence in children.
the frequency of RTE T cells is a good indicator of ART adherence.
